sections.h2: Where is Derby, Kansas, and how did it start?
sections.html:
Derby is a city in Sedgwick County and the largest suburb of Wichita, lying south of the city next to McConnell Air Force Base. The 2020 census counted 25,625 residents, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 26,606.

The city's own history page says the Alexander Garrett family stopped a covered wagon on the bank of Spring Creek in the spring of 1869 after a trip from Ohio. Wikipedia adds that the community was platted in 1871 as El Paso, after El Paso, Illinois. In 1880 the Santa Fe railway renamed its station Derby, after a railroad official, to avoid confusion with El Paso, Texas, and the city officially took that name in 1956.

Aircraft manufacturing, the Air Force base and the school district are the anchors. Wikipedia's Derby article names Textron Aviation and other aircraft makers among local employers, along with Derby Public Schools and McConnell Air Force Base, and says the city supports more than 532 businesses.

It lists construction, retail, finance, insurance, real estate and health care as the strongest sectors. Smaller manufacturers such as BRG Precision Products and Mid Continent Controls are also named.

McConnell took its name in April 1954 from two of the three Flying McConnell brothers of Wichita, and the Air Force describes it as a significant hub for the service. A household with orders to move on a set date may not have months to wait for a listing to sell.

Derby Public Schools, USD 260, serves Derby, McConnell Air Force Base, the Oaklawn Improvement District and some southern parts of Wichita, according to the city's history page. That means a Wichita mailing address does not guarantee Wichita schools.

The Air Force housing office says the district operates a sixth grade center, a middle school, a high school and an alternative high school in addition to its elementary schools. Wineteer Elementary is the school for McConnell family housing. Derby High School offers Advanced Placement and honors classes, and a latch key program covers before and after school care.

Wikipedia also lists two private schools in the city, St. Mary Catholic School and Faith Lutheran School. Neighboring districts include Haysville USD 261, Mulvane USD 263, Goddard USD 265 and Andover USD 385, which matters if your house is near a boundary.

sections.h2: What permits does the City of Derby require before you sell or repair?
sections.html:
Derby requires permits for many projects, and contractors must be licensed by the city. A city development director's column from March 2024 lists the kinds of work that need one.

  • Fences, decks, garages, pools, sheds, pergolas, gazebos and outdoor kitchens.
  • Most electrical, plumbing and heating or air conditioning work.
  • Driveway approaches, retaining walls, sprinkler systems and wells.
  • Roofing and siding replacement over 400 square feet.
  • Anything built in a flood plain also needs a Flood Plain Development Permit.

The city notes that inspections catch problems such as an improperly installed water heater, faulty wiring or a deck built below code. To find out whether a contractor is licensed, call the city at 788-6632 or email permits@derbyweb.com. Inspections must be requested 24 hours ahead on the residential permit form.

If you are selling a house where a past owner finished a basement or added a deck without a permit, a buyer's inspector may ask about it. Pulling records from the city before you list can save a deal from stalling.

sections.h2: How does a house sale in Derby, Kansas work?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or take a cash offer. A listing usually involves repairs, showings and a buyer's lender, while a cash buyer can skip the loan step.

Kansas rules treat the deed as the transfer document. Sedgwick County says deeds are filed with the Register of Deeds along with a Real Estate Sales Validation Questionnaire, and the County Clerk then updates the tax record. For a Derby parcel, the Sedgwick County Treasurer bills the tax, with payment due December 20 for the full amount or first half and May 10 for the second half.

  • Ask the Treasurer for the current balance before you set a closing date.
  • Check for special assessments with the City of Derby or the County Clerk.
  • Gather permit records for any work done on the house.

sections.h2: Does Derby face weather risks that affect a house sale?
sections.html:
Derby has a humid subtropical climate, with hot, humid summers and generally mild to cool winters, according to Wikipedia's climate summary. The page does not give hail or flood figures, so rely on a home inspection and your insurer for those.

Because the city's permit rules mention a Flood Plain Development Permit, check whether your lot falls in a mapped flood area before you assume nothing is required.

The city's permit office, at 788-6632, is the place to ask about flood plain mapping for your address.

sections.h2: What do Derby sellers commonly deal with?
sections.html:
Based on the city's permit rules and the area's military connection, these are the issues to prepare for.

  • A short timeline because of a military move or a job change.
  • Unpermitted work that a buyer's inspector flags.
  • Delinquent property tax, which the county Treasurer can pursue through foreclosure after roughly two and a half years.
  • Inherited houses where the family wants a quick sale without staging or repairs.

If one of these fits you, send us the address of your Derby house. We will explain how a cash offer could work and what the closing steps would be.

sections.h2: How do you get around Derby?
sections.html:
Derby is served by the Derby Dash, which gives point to point bus rides inside city limits, and the Wichita metro area is reachable by road. The city has parks such as High Park, with fishing, soccer fields and an amphitheatre, plus Rock River Rapids Aquatic Park.

Those amenities appear in Wikipedia's article on the city.

sections.h2: How do Derby homeowners handle a Sedgwick County valuation or a tax problem?
sections.html:
Derby parcels are valued by the Sedgwick County Appraiser, not by the city. Valuation notices go out March 1, and an informal appeal must be returned within 30 days, usually by March 31. A value can be appealed only once per tax year.

If taxes fall behind, the county Treasurer eventually lists parcels that are two and a half or three and a half years delinquent for foreclosure, and a $400 foreclosure fee was added on October 1, 2026 for the current list. Paying in full ends the case, and an owner can redeem up to the close of business the day before the auction.

A cash sale that pays off the balance at closing can resolve the lien. Whoever handles your sale should ask the Treasurer, at 316-660-9000, for an up to date payoff before the closing date is set.

sections.h2: What should you gather before talking to a Derby cash buyer?
sections.html:
A short folder of documents speeds things up. None of it is required to ask for an offer, but it helps answer the buyer's first questions.

  • The deed or a recent tax statement showing the legal owner.
  • Permit records for additions, a new roof, a deck or a finished basement.
  • Any notice from the county about delinquent tax or special assessments.
  • A note on whether the house is occupied by you, a tenant or no one.

With those in hand, the conversation about timing and price is more concrete.

faqs.q: How many people live in Derby, KS?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau counted 25,625 people in the 2020 census, and its July 1, 2025 estimate is 26,606.

faqs.q: Which school district covers Derby, Kansas?
faqs.a: Derby Public Schools, USD 260, serves the city, McConnell Air Force Base, the Oaklawn Improvement District and some southern Wichita neighborhoods.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a roof in Derby?
faqs.a: Roofing and siding replacements over 400 square feet need a permit, according to a City of Derby development director's column. Call 788-6632 to confirm for your project.

faqs.q: When is property tax due on a Derby house?
faqs.a: The Sedgwick County Treasurer bills it. Full payment or the first half is due December 20, and the second half is due May 10.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Derby house as-is for cash?
faqs.a: Yes. You can accept a cash offer instead of listing, and the buyer may take the house as it stands. Send us the address and we will explain the steps.
